q: Within a plant, mineral ions and organic compounds (e.g., sucrose) are transported by being dissolved in ____.
e: Within a plant, mineral ions and organic compounds (e.g., sucrose) are transported by being dissolved in water. That missing piece is water.

q: The dissolved mineral ions are transported in the xylem tissue and the dissolved organic compounds are transported in the ____ tissue.
e: The dissolved mineral ions are transported in the xylem tissue and the dissolved organic compounds are transported in the phloem tissue. That missing piece is phloem.

q: The plant roots are responsible for the uptake of water and mineral ions and can have ____ to increase the surface area for absorption of the substances.
e: The plant roots are responsible for the uptake of water and mineral ions and can have root hairs to increase the surface area for absorption of the substances. That missing piece is root hairs.

q: The uptake of water is a ____ process and occurs by osmosis (the diffusion of water from a higher water potential to a lower water potential).
e: The uptake of water is a passive process and occurs by osmosis (the diffusion of water from a higher water potential to a lower water potential). The blank is passive.

q: The uptake of minerals can be passive transport such as diffusion and osmosis, and/or ____ transport.
e: The uptake of minerals can be passive transport such as diffusion and osmosis, and/or active transport. That missing piece is active.

q: In the active absorption, the water first enters the ____ and passes from one cell to another.
e: In the active absorption, the water first enters the cell sap and passes from one cell to another. That missing piece is cell sap.

q: This type of movement where protoplasm is involved is called ____.
e: This type of movement where protoplasm is involved is called symplast. Write symplast in the gap.

q: In passive absorption, water moves through the ____ of the root.
e: In passive absorption, water moves through the apoplast of the root. The blank is apoplast.

q: The apoplast path includes the ____ and intercellular spaces.
e: The apoplast path includes the cell wall and intercellular spaces. That missing piece is cell wall.

q: Most water travels via the ____ pathway (when transpiration rates are high), which is the series of spaces running through the cellulose cell walls, dead cells, and the hollow tubes of the xylem.
e: Most water travels via the apoplastic pathway (when transpiration rates are high), which is the series of spaces running through the cellulose cell walls, dead cells, and the hollow tubes of the xylem. Write apoplastic in the gap.

q: The water moves by ____ (as it does not pass through a partially permeable membrane) in the apoplastic pathway.
e: The water moves by diffusion (as it does not pass through a partially permeable membrane) in the apoplastic pathway. The blank is diffusion.

q: When the water reaches the endodermis the presence of a thick, waterproof, waxy band of ____ within the cell wall blocks the apoplastic pathway.
e: When the water reaches the endodermis the presence of a thick, waterproof, waxy band of suberin within the cell wall blocks the apoplastic pathway. The blank is suberin.

q: A smaller amount of water travels via the ____ pathway, which is the cytoplasm and plasmodesmata or vacuole of the cells.
e: A smaller amount of water travels via the symplastic pathway, which is the cytoplasm and plasmodesmata or vacuole of the cells. That missing piece is symplastic.

q: The water moves by osmosis into the cell, possibly into the vacuole (through the tonoplast by osmosis) and between cells through the ____.
e: The water moves by osmosis into the cell, possibly into the vacuole (through the tonoplast by osmosis) and between cells through the plasmodesmata. The blank is plasmodesmata.

q: The cells in the ____ layers are not tightly packed and have many spaces around them filled with air.
e: The cells in the mesophyll layers are not tightly packed and have many spaces around them filled with air. That missing piece is mesophyll.

q: The walls of the mesophyll cells are wet and some of this water evaporates into the air space, so that the air inside the leaf is usually ____ with water vapour.
e: The walls of the mesophyll cells are wet and some of this water evaporates into the air space, so that the air inside the leaf is usually saturated with water vapour. The blank is saturated.

q: The air in the internal spaces of the leaf has directly contacted with the air outside the leaf, through small pores called ____.
e: The air in the internal spaces of the leaf has directly contacted with the air outside the leaf, through small pores called stomata. That missing piece is stomata.

q: If there is a ____ between the air inside the leaf (higher water potential) and the air outside of the leaf (lower water potential), then water vapour will diffuse out of the leaf down this gradient.
e: If there is a water potential gradient between the air inside the leaf (higher water potential) and the air outside of the leaf (lower water potential), then water vapour will diffuse out of the leaf down this gradient. The blank is water potential gradient.

q: In condition of low ____, the gradient is steep, so transpiration takes place more quickly than in high humidity.
e: In condition of low humidity, the gradient is steep, so transpiration takes place more quickly than in high humidity. That missing piece is humidity.

q: Transpiration rate may also be increased by an increasing in ____ or rising in temperature.
e: Transpiration rate may also be increased by an increasing in wind speed or rising in temperature. That missing piece is wind speed.

q: In most plants, stomata open during the day and close at ____.
e: In most plants, stomata open during the day and close at night. Write night in the gap.

q: Stomata must be opened during the day to allow ____ to diffuse into the leaf for photosynthesis.
e: Stomata must be opened during the day to allow carbon dioxide to diffuse into the leaf for photosynthesis. That missing piece is carbon dioxide.

q: In especially dry conditions, when the water potential gradient between the internal air spaces and the external air is steep, a plant may have to compromise by partially or completely closing its ____ to prevent its leaves drying out.
e: In especially dry conditions, when the water potential gradient between the internal air spaces and the external air is steep, a plant may have to compromise by partially or completely closing its stomata to prevent its leaves drying out. That missing piece is stomata.

q: In hot conditions, transpiration plays an important role in ____ the leaves.
e: In hot conditions, transpiration plays an important role in cooling the leaves. Write cooling in the gap.

q: If the rate at which water vapour is lost by transpiration ____ the rate at which a plant can take up water from the soil, then the amount of water in its cells decreases.
e: If the rate at which water vapour is lost by transpiration exceeds the rate at which a plant can take up water from the soil, then the amount of water in its cells decreases. Write exceeds in the gap.

q: The cells become less turgid and the plant ____ as the soft parts such as leaves loose the support provided turgid cells.
e: The cells become less turgid and the plant wilts as the soft parts such as leaves loose the support provided turgid cells. The blank is wilts.

q: Ascent of sap mostly occurs due to ____ exerted transpiration of water.
e: Ascent of sap mostly occurs due to transpiration pull exerted transpiration of water. That missing piece is transpiration pull.

q: The development of ____ tissue, which is essential for providing rigidity and strength to the plant, is favoured by the increase in transpiration.
e: The development of mechanical tissue, which is essential for providing rigidity and strength to the plant, is favoured by the increase in transpiration. That missing piece is mechanical.

q: Mineral salts are mostly distributed by rising column of ____.
e: Mineral salts are mostly distributed by rising column of sap. Write sap in the gap.

q: Transpiration helps in better development of ____ system, which is required for support, and absorption of mineral salts.
e: Transpiration helps in better development of root system, which is required for support, and absorption of mineral salts. The blank is root.

q: The ash and ____ content of the fruit increases with the increase in transpiration.
e: The ash and sugar content of the fruit increases with the increase in transpiration. Write sugar in the gap.

q: Excessive transpiration induces hardening and resistant to moderate ____.
e: Excessive transpiration induces hardening and resistant to moderate drought. The blank is drought.

q: Transpiration helps the shape and structure of plant parts by keeping cells ____.
e: Transpiration helps the shape and structure of plant parts by keeping cells turgid. Write turgid in the gap.

q: As water evaporates through the stomata, it results in pulling of water, molecule by molecule into the leaf from the ____.
e: As water evaporates through the stomata, it results in pulling of water, molecule by molecule into the leaf from the xylem. That missing piece is xylem.

q: A ____ funnel is filled with water and rubber stopper attaches a leafy twig to it in the demonstration of transpiration pull.
e: A thistle funnel is filled with water and rubber stopper attaches a leafy twig to it in the demonstration of transpiration pull. The blank is thistle.

q: Loss of water from the twig(i.e., transpiration) produces a ____ in the thistle funnel and water will be drawn up.
e: Loss of water from the twig(i.e., transpiration) produces a vacuum in the thistle funnel and water will be drawn up. That missing piece is vacuum.

q: ____ is the movement of dissolved substances through a plant.
e: Translocation is the movement of dissolved substances through a plant. The blank is Translocation.

q: In general, water and dissolved salts from the soil travel upwards through the vessels of the xylem and food synthesized in the leaves passes downwards or upwards in the ____ of the phloem.
e: In general, water and dissolved salts from the soil travel upwards through the vessels of the xylem and food synthesized in the leaves passes downwards or upwards in the sieve tubes of the phloem. The blank is sieve tubes.

q: When leaves photosynthesize, they produce ____.
e: When leaves photosynthesize, they produce carbohydrates. That missing piece is carbohydrates.

q: These carbohydrates are transported out of the leaf in the form of ____ to the stem.
e: These carbohydrates are transported out of the leaf in the form of sucrose to the stem. That missing piece is sucrose.

q: Once in the stem it may travel upwards to actively growing regions or maturing fruits and seeds or downwards to the roots and underground ____ organs.
e: Once in the stem it may travel upwards to actively growing regions or maturing fruits and seeds or downwards to the roots and underground storage organs. Write storage in the gap.

q: Both upward and downward movement may take place at the ____ time in the phloem.
e: Both upward and downward movement may take place at the same time in the phloem. Write same in the gap.

q: The phloem tissue is a ____ tissue.
e: The phloem tissue is a complex tissue. The blank is complex.

q: The consisting components are sieve tube, ____ cell, phloem parenchyma and phloem fibre.
e: The consisting components are sieve tube, companion cell, phloem parenchyma and phloem fibre. Write companion in the gap.

q: Sieve cells can manage translocation without nuclei because they are kept alive by the nucleated ____ cells that always situated adjacent to sieve cells.
e: Sieve cells can manage translocation without nuclei because they are kept alive by the nucleated companion cells that always situated adjacent to sieve cells. Write companion in the gap.

q: Moreover, phloem tissue is strengthened by ____ cells besides the sieve and companion cells.
e: Moreover, phloem tissue is strengthened by fibre cells besides the sieve and companion cells. Write fibre in the gap.

q: Large multicellular animals have evolved transport system as organisms get larger and have higher ____ rates.
e: Large multicellular animals have evolved transport system as organisms get larger and have higher metabolic rates. That missing piece is metabolic.

q: In many large animals, including all the vertebrates, circulatory system is in the form of ____ transport system.
e: In many large animals, including all the vertebrates, circulatory system is in the form of mass transport system. The blank is mass.

q: Mass transport system is an arrangement of structures by which substances are transported in the flow of a ____ with a mechanism for moving it around the body.
e: Mass transport system is an arrangement of structures by which substances are transported in the flow of a fluid with a mechanism for moving it around the body. The blank is fluid.

q: Single-celled organisms have a high ____.
e: Single-celled organisms have a high surface area to volume ratio. Write surface area to volume ratio in the gap.

q: In large multicellular organisms, the surface area to volume ratio is ____.
e: In large multicellular organisms, the surface area to volume ratio is low. The blank is low.

q: Respiration supplies energy for the other reactions of life, but it also produces the toxic waste product ____.
e: Respiration supplies energy for the other reactions of life, but it also produces the toxic waste product carbon dioxide. The blank is carbon dioxide.

q: Most mass transport systems have certain similar features as follow: ____ surfaces to get materials into and out of the transport system.
e: Most mass transport systems have certain similar features as follow: exchange surfaces to get materials into and out of the transport system. Write exchange in the gap.

q: a way of moving materials fast enough to supply the needs of the organism - this may involve mechanical methods such as the pumping of the ____.
e: a way of moving materials fast enough to supply the needs of the organism - this may involve mechanical methods such as the pumping of the heart. The blank is heart.

q: a suitable transport ____ (e.g., fluid).
e: a suitable transport medium (e.g., fluid). Write medium in the gap.

q: There are two main types of circulatory system; open circulatory system and ____ circulatory system.
e: There are two main types of circulatory system; open circulatory system and closed circulatory system. The blank is closed.

q: Open circulatory system - Blood pumped by the ____ heart leaves the open-ended vessels to a series of blood spaces surrounding the tissues.
e: Open circulatory system - Blood pumped by the tubular heart leaves the open-ended vessels to a series of blood spaces surrounding the tissues. Write tubular in the gap.

q: When the heart relaxes, the blood flow back into the vessels through pores called ____.
e: When the heart relaxes, the blood flow back into the vessels through pores called ostia. The blank is ostia.

q: This type is found in most ____ (jointed leg animals such as insects, spiders and crabs).
e: This type is found in most arthropods (jointed leg animals such as insects, spiders and crabs). The blank is arthropods.

q: Closed circulatory system- Blood is pumped by the heart into the ____ which carry the blood to the tissues of the entire body.
e: Closed circulatory system- Blood is pumped by the heart into the blood vessels which carry the blood to the tissues of the entire body. That missing piece is blood vessels.

q: The main advantages of a closed system are- (i) the ____ can be increased to make the blood flow more quickly.
e: The main advantages of a closed system are- (i) the pressure can be increased to make the blood flow more quickly. Write pressure in the gap.

q: Single circulatory system- It is found in ____.
e: Single circulatory system- It is found in fish. Write fish in the gap.

q: The heart pumps deoxygenated blood to the ____, the organs of gas exchange where the blood takes in oxygen.
e: The heart pumps deoxygenated blood to the gills, the organs of gas exchange where the blood takes in oxygen. Write gills in the gap.

q: In this type, blood passes ____ through the heart.
e: In this type, blood passes once through the heart. The blank is once.

q: Double circulatory system- Birds and mammals have evolved the most complex type of transport system, known as a ____ circulatory system because it involves two separate circulations.
e: Double circulatory system- Birds and mammals have evolved the most complex type of transport system, known as a double circulatory system because it involves two separate circulations. The blank is double.

q: The ____ circulation carries oxygenated blood (oxygen-rich blood) from the heart to the cells of the body where the oxygen is used.
e: The systemic circulation carries oxygenated blood (oxygen-rich blood) from the heart to the cells of the body where the oxygen is used. The blank is systemic.

q: The ____ circulation carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs to be oxygenated and then carries the oxygenated blood back to the heart.
e: The pulmonary circulation carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs to be oxygenated and then carries the oxygenated blood back to the heart. That missing piece is pulmonary.

q: Thus, blood passes ____ through the heart.
e: Thus, blood passes twice through the heart. Write twice in the gap.

q: Birds and mammals need much more ____ than fish.
e: Birds and mammals need much more oxygen than fish. The blank is oxygen.

q: The separate circuits of a double circulatory system ensure that the oxygenated and deoxygenated blood cannot ____.
e: The separate circuits of a double circulatory system ensure that the oxygenated and deoxygenated blood cannot mix. Write mix in the gap.

q: The fully oxygenated blood can be delivered quickly to the body tissues at high ____.
e: The fully oxygenated blood can be delivered quickly to the body tissues at high pressure. The blank is pressure.

q: The blood going through the tiny blood vessels in the lungs is at relatively ____ pressure, so it does not damage the vessels and allows gas exchange to take place.
e: The blood going through the tiny blood vessels in the lungs is at relatively low pressure, so it does not damage the vessels and allows gas exchange to take place. Write low in the gap.

q: In mammals, the cardiovascular system delivers the materials needed by the cells of the body, and carries away the waste products of their ____.
e: In mammals, the cardiovascular system delivers the materials needed by the cells of the body, and carries away the waste products of their metabolism. That missing piece is metabolism.

q: The cardiovascular system is made up of the heart- which acts as a ____ to move blood through the vessels, a series of blood vessels- which carry blood and the blood - as transport medium.
e: The cardiovascular system is made up of the heart- which acts as a pump to move blood through the vessels, a series of blood vessels- which carry blood and the blood - as transport medium. Write pump in the gap.

q: The human heart, like other mammalian hearts, is a muscular pump with ____ chambers.
e: The human heart, like other mammalian hearts, is a muscular pump with four chambers. The blank is four.

q: The upper two chambers are called the right ____ and the left atrium.
e: The upper two chambers are called the right atrium and the left atrium. The blank is atrium.

q: The lower chambers are the right ____ and the left ventricle.
e: The lower chambers are the right ventricle and the left ventricle. That missing piece is ventricle.

q: The walls of the atria are ____ than those of the ventricles.
e: The walls of the atria are thinner than those of the ventricles. The blank is thinner.

q: The right atrium receives the blood from the ____ which collects deoxygenated blood from the head, neck, arms and chest.
e: The right atrium receives the blood from the superior vena cava which collects deoxygenated blood from the head, neck, arms and chest. That missing piece is superior vena cava.

q: ...and from the ____ which receives deoxygenated blood from the lower parts of the body.
e: ..and from the inferior vena cava which receives deoxygenated blood from the lower parts of the body. Write inferior vena cava in the gap.

q: The left atrium receives oxygenated blood from the lungs via ____.
e: The left atrium receives oxygenated blood from the lungs via pulmonary veins. The blank is pulmonary veins.

q: After the blood enters into both ventricles from the corresponding atrium, the deoxygenated blood in right ventricle enters the lungs through ____.
e: After the blood enters into both ventricles from the corresponding atrium, the deoxygenated blood in right ventricle enters the lungs through pulmonary artery. That missing piece is pulmonary artery.

q: The oxygenated blood in the left ventricle enters into ____ and then passes throughout the body.
e: The oxygenated blood in the left ventricle enters into aorta and then passes throughout the body. That missing piece is aorta.

q: As the two sides are separated by a complete thick, muscular ____, the blood in one side of the heart does not mix with the blood from the other side.
e: As the two sides are separated by a complete thick, muscular septum, the blood in one side of the heart does not mix with the blood from the other side. That missing piece is septum.

q: The heart is made of a unique type of muscle, known as ____ muscle, which has special properties, it can carry on contracting regularly without resting or getting fatigued.
e: The heart is made of a unique type of muscle, known as cardiac muscle, which has special properties, it can carry on contracting regularly without resting or getting fatigued. That missing piece is cardiac.

q: Cardiac muscle has a good blood supply by the ____ arteries bringing oxygenated blood while coronary veins carry away the deoxygenated blood.
e: Cardiac muscle has a good blood supply by the coronary arteries bringing oxygenated blood while coronary veins carry away the deoxygenated blood. That missing piece is coronary.

q: The muscular wall of the left ventricle is much ____ than that of the right.
e: The muscular wall of the left ventricle is much thicker than that of the right. Write thicker in the gap.

q: The right ventricle pumps blood to the ____, which are relatively close to the heart.
e: The right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs, which are relatively close to the heart. Write lungs in the gap.

q: The delicate capillaries of the lungs need blood delivered at relatively ____ pressure.
e: The delicate capillaries of the lungs need blood delivered at relatively low pressure. The blank is low.

q: The left ventricle must produce sufficient force to move the blood under pressure to all the extremities of the body and overcome the elastic ____ of the arteries.
e: The left ventricle must produce sufficient force to move the blood under pressure to all the extremities of the body and overcome the elastic recoil of the arteries. Write recoil in the gap.

q: The right atrioventricular valve is called ____ valves which is made up of three flaps and is located between the right atrium and right ventricle.
e: The right atrioventricular valve is called tricuspid valves which is made up of three flaps and is located between the right atrium and right ventricle. Write tricuspid in the gap.

q: The left atrioventricular valve is called ____ valve (Mitral valve) which is made up of two flaps and is located between the left atrium and left ventricle.
e: The left atrioventricular valve is called bicuspid valve (Mitral valve) which is made up of two flaps and is located between the left atrium and left ventricle. That missing piece is bicuspid.

q: The flaps of both atrioventricular valves are supported by the ____ (tendinous cords) which prevent the flaps from turning inside out by the pressure exerted when the ventricles contract.
e: The flaps of both atrioventricular valves are supported by the cordae tendineae (tendinous cords) which prevent the flaps from turning inside out by the pressure exerted when the ventricles contract. That missing piece is cordae tendineae.

q: ____ valves (semi means half and lunar means moon)- Both are pocket-like valves with half-moon shaped like those in veins.
e: Semilunar valves (semi means half and lunar means moon)- Both are pocket-like valves with half-moon shaped like those in veins. The blank is Semilunar.

q: One set is located at the base of the pulmonary artery while the other set is at the base of the ____.
e: One set is located at the base of the pulmonary artery while the other set is at the base of the aorta. The blank is aorta.

q: Arteries carry blood ____ from the heart towards the cells of the body.
e: Arteries carry blood away from the heart towards the cells of the body. That missing piece is away.

q: Almost all arteries carry ____ blood.
e: Almost all arteries carry oxygenated blood. Write oxygenated in the gap.

q: The exceptions are: the pulmonary artery-carrying deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs and the ____ artery - during pregnancy, this carries deoxygenated blood from the foetus to the placenta.
e: The exceptions are: the pulmonary artery-carrying deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs and the umbilical artery - during pregnancy, this carries deoxygenated blood from the foetus to the placenta. The blank is umbilical.

q: The very smallest branches of the arterial system, furthest from the heart, are the ____.
e: The very smallest branches of the arterial system, furthest from the heart, are the arterioles. Write arterioles in the gap.

q: Their walls contain a lot of ____ fibers so they can stretch to accommodate the greater volume of blood without being damaged.
e: Their walls contain a lot of elastic fibers so they can stretch to accommodate the greater volume of blood without being damaged. Write elastic in the gap.

q: The role of the elastic fibers in artery walls is to return to their original length to help ____ the pressure.
e: The role of the elastic fibers in artery walls is to return to their original length to help maintain the pressure. The blank is maintain.

q: A thick muscular wall helps control the flow of blood by dilating (widening) or ____ (narrowing) the vessels.
e: A thick muscular wall helps control the flow of blood by dilating (widening) or constricting (narrowing) the vessels. Write constricting in the gap.

q: Veins carry blood ____ towards the heart.
e: Veins carry blood back towards the heart. Write back in the gap.

q: Most veins carry ____ blood.
e: Most veins carry deoxygenated blood. That missing piece is deoxygenated.

q: The exceptions are: the ____ vein, carries oxygen-rich blood from the lungs back to the heart for circulation around the body.
e: The exceptions are: the pulmonary vein, carries oxygen-rich blood from the lungs back to the heart for circulation around the body. Write pulmonary in the gap.

q: Tiny ____ lead from the capillary network, combining into larger and larger vessels going back to the heart as vena cava (large vein).
e: Tiny venules lead from the capillary network, combining into larger and larger vessels going back to the heart as vena cava (large vein). That missing piece is venules.

q: Veins can hold a large volume of blood, in fact more than ____ of the body's blood volume is in the veins at any one time.
e: Veins can hold a large volume of blood, in fact more than half of the body's blood volume is in the veins at any one time. The blank is half.

q: The walls of the veins are ____ than those of the arteries and contain less elastic tissue and muscle.
e: The walls of the veins are thinner than those of the arteries and contain less elastic tissue and muscle. The blank is thinner.

q: There are ____ valves at frequent intervals throughout the venous system.
e: There are one-way valves at frequent intervals throughout the venous system. The blank is one-way.

q: The contraction of large ____ encourages blood flow through the veins.
e: The contraction of large muscles encourages blood flow through the veins. The blank is muscles.

q: ____ have a very simple structure which is well adapted to their function.
e: Capillaries have a very simple structure which is well adapted to their function. That missing piece is Capillaries.

q: Their walls are very thin and contain no elastic fibers, smooth muscle or ____.
e: Their walls are very thin and contain no elastic fibers, smooth muscle or collagen. That missing piece is collagen.

q: The walls consist of just ____ very thin cell.
e: The walls consist of just one very thin cell. Write one in the gap.

q: Blood entering the capillary network from the arteries is ____.
e: Blood entering the capillary network from the arteries is oxygenated. Write oxygenated in the gap.

q: ____ is the liquid part of the blood.
e: Plasma is the liquid part of the blood. That missing piece is Plasma.

q: Over $50\%$ of the blood volume in the body is ____, and it carries all of blood cells and everything else that needs transporting around the body.
e: Over 50\% of the blood volume in the body is plasma, and it carries all of blood cells and everything else that needs transporting around the body. That missing piece is plasma.

q: Mature erythrocytes do not contain a ____ and have a limited life of about 120 days.
e: Mature erythrocytes do not contain a nucleus and have a limited life of about 120 days. The blank is nucleus.

q: The ____ disc shape of the cells means that they have a large surface area to volume ratio, so oxygen can diffuse into and out of them rapidly.
e: The biconcave disc shape of the cells means that they have a large surface area to volume ratio, so oxygen can diffuse into and out of them rapidly. That missing piece is biconcave.

q: Leucocytes or white blood cells... They are much larger than erythrocytes but can also squeeze through tiny blood vessels because they can change their ____.
e: Leucocytes or white blood cells.. They are much larger than erythrocytes but can also squeeze through tiny blood vessels because they can change their shape. That missing piece is shape.

q: Their main function is to defend the body against ____.
e: Their main function is to defend the body against infection. The blank is infection.

q: Leucocytes are also very important in the ____ response of the body when an area of tissue is damaged.
e: Leucocytes are also very important in the inflammatory response of the body when an area of tissue is damaged. Write inflammatory in the gap.

q: Platelets are tiny fragments of large cells called ____, which are found in the bone marrow.
e: Platelets are tiny fragments of large cells called megakaryocytes, which are found in the bone marrow. That missing piece is megakaryocytes.

q: Contact between the platelets and components of the tissue (e.g., ____ fibres in the skin) causes the platelets to break open in large numbers.
e: Contact between the platelets and components of the tissue (e.g., collagen fibres in the skin) causes the platelets to break open in large numbers. The blank is collagen.

q: ____ causes the smooth muscle of the blood vessel to contract.
e: Serotonin causes the smooth muscle of the blood vessel to contract. That missing piece is Serotonin.

q: ____ is an enzyme that starts a sequence of chemical changes that clot the blood.
e: Thromboplastin is an enzyme that starts a sequence of chemical changes that clot the blood. Write Thromboplastin in the gap.

q: Vitamin K is important in the production of many of the compounds needed for the blood to clot, including ____.
e: Vitamin K is important in the production of many of the compounds needed for the blood to clot, including prothrombin. That missing piece is prothrombin.

q: First, thromboplastin catalyses the conversion of a large soluble protein called prothrombin found in the plasma into another soluble protein, the enzyme called ____.
e: First, thromboplastin catalyses the conversion of a large soluble protein called prothrombin found in the plasma into another soluble protein, the enzyme called thrombin. That missing piece is thrombin.

q: ____ ions need to be present in the blood at the right concentration for this reaction to happen.
e: Calcium ions need to be present in the blood at the right concentration for this reaction to happen. The blank is Calcium.

q: Second, thrombin acts on another soluble plasma protein called fibrinogen, converting it to an insoluble substance called ____.
e: Second, thrombin acts on another soluble plasma protein called fibrinogen, converting it to an insoluble substance called fibrin. Write fibrin in the gap.

q: Finally, the fibrin forms a ____ of fibres to cover the wound and trap the red blood cells, forming blood clot.
e: Finally, the fibrin forms a mesh of fibres to cover the wound and trap the red blood cells, forming blood clot. The blank is mesh.

q: The contractions of the heart are called ____.
e: The contractions of the heart are called systole. The blank is systole.

q: Systole can be divided into atrial systole, the contraction of atria and the ____ systole, the contraction of ventricles.
e: Systole can be divided into atrial systole, the contraction of atria and the ventricular systole, the contraction of ventricles. The blank is ventricular.

q: Ventricular systole happens about $0.13$ seconds after ____ systole.
e: Ventricular systole happens about 0.13 seconds after atrial systole. The blank is atrial.

q: Between contractions the heart ____ and fills with blood.
e: Between contractions the heart relaxes and fills with blood. The blank is relaxes.

q: One cycle of systole and diastole makes up a single heartbeat, which lasts about $0.8$ seconds in humans.
e: One cycle of systole and diastole makes up a single heartbeat, which lasts about 0.8 seconds in humans. The blank is 0.8.

q: Cardiac muscle cells are ____, which means they contract without any external stimulus.
e: Cardiac muscle cells are myogenic, which means they contract without any external stimulus. That missing piece is myogenic.

q: The intrinsic rhythm of the heart is around $60$ beats per minute which is slower than the heartbeat most of the time when awake.
e: The intrinsic rhythm of the heart is around 60 beats per minute which is slower than the heartbeat most of the time when awake. That missing piece is 60.

q: The area of the heart with the fastest intrinsic rhythm is a group of cells in the right atrium known as the ____, and this acts as the heart's own natural pacemaker which keeps the heart beating regularly.
e: The area of the heart with the fastest intrinsic rhythm is a group of cells in the right atrium known as the sinoatrial node, and this acts as the heart's own natural pacemaker which keeps the heart beating regularly. Write sinoatrial node in the gap.

q: Excitation also spreads to another area of similar tissue called the ____.
e: Excitation also spreads to another area of similar tissue called the atrioventricular node. The blank is atrioventricular node.

q: The AVN is excited as a result of the SAN but it produces a slight delay before the wave of depolarization passes into the ____, a group of conducting fibres in the septum of the heart.
e: The AVN is excited as a result of the SAN but it produces a slight delay before the wave of depolarization passes into the bundle of His, a group of conducting fibres in the septum of the heart. Write bundle of His in the gap.

q: The bundle of His splits into two branches and carries the wave of excitation to the ____ tissue.
e: The bundle of His splits into two branches and carries the wave of excitation to the purkyne tissue. That missing piece is purkyne.

q: These electrical changes can be measured in an ____ (ECG).
e: These electrical changes can be measured in an electrocardiogram (ECG). That missing piece is electrocardiogram.

q: Between the capillaries and the cells is a watery liquid called ____.
e: Between the capillaries and the cells is a watery liquid called tissue fluid. The blank is tissue fluid.

q: Most of the water from tissue fluid reenters capillaries by ____.
e: Most of the water from tissue fluid reenters capillaries by osmosis. That missing piece is osmosis.

q: Some fluid passes into another system called the ____ system.
e: Some fluid passes into another system called the lymphatic system. That missing piece is lymphatic.

q: The ____ that carry fats from villi of the small intestine are part of the lymphatic system.
e: The lacteals that carry fats from villi of the small intestine are part of the lymphatic system. That missing piece is lacteals.

q: Before lymph passes back into the blood, it is ____ to remove dead cells and bacteria.
e: Before lymph passes back into the blood, it is filtered to remove dead cells and bacteria. That missing piece is filtered.
